Dyslexia Assistant • Product Overview Executive Summary

1. Executive Summary & Clinical Foundations

Dyslexia affects an estimated 10% to 20% of the global population, representing the most prevalent neurodevelopmental learning difference. Common symptoms include visual crowding, dancing or vibrating letters, phonological processing lag, and severe eye strain triggered by high-contrast black text on stark white backgrounds.

The Problem with Conventional Software:

Mainstream e-readers and word processors are designed for neurotypical readers. They lack contrast shields, ignore letter weighting, present overwhelming UI clutter, and require constant high-speed cloud connections that risk student data privacy.

The Dyslexia Assistant Solution:

A calming, zero-distraction workspace equipped with scientifically proven fonts (Lexend, OpenDyslexic), 8 pastel tint overlays, bionic syllable breaking, reading rulers, and integrated audio synthesis.

2. Core Architectural Principles

Pillar Implementation Clinical & Practical Value
Offline-First Architecture Service Worker PWA, IndexedDB & LocalStorage Zero student data leaves the browser. Works seamlessly in low-connectivity rural schools and air-gapped exams.
Visual Fatigue Elimination 8 Pastel Tints & High-Contrast Guard (>4.5:1) Softens harsh screen glare (Irlen syndrome), stabilizing ocular fixation and reducing reading headaches.
Cognitive Anchoring OpenDyslexic Gravity Weights & Bionic Bold Anchors the bottom of characters, preventing mental rotation and flipping of confusing letters (b vs d, p vs q).
Auditory Reinforcement SpeechSynthesis API & Focus Soundscapes Bridges the phoneme-grapheme divide through dual-modality reading and ambient noise masking.

Dyslexia Assistant • Visual Accommodations Reader Engine

3. The Clinical Reader Engine

The core Reader module allows users to import raw text, documents (.txt, .pdf, .docx), or select from curated literature. The text is immediately transformed using personalized visual accommodations.

Scientifically Backed Typography

  • Lexend Deca: Engineered specifically to maximize reading speed by expanding character spacing.
  • OpenDyslexic: Weighted bottoms prevent letters from flipping or rotating in the reader's visual cortex.
  • Atkinson Hyperlegible: Distinct letterforms designed to eliminate character ambiguity.

Reading Ruler Focus Mask

Moving the mouse or arrow keys navigates a translucent focus window that dims lines above and below the active sentence. This isolates the reader's foveal field, eliminating ocular drifting.

Bionic & Syllable Processing

  • Bionic Reading: Automatically bolds the first 3 letters of each word, guiding the eye through fixation saccades.
  • Syllable Splitting: Hyphenates complex, multisyllabic words (e.g., com-pu-ta-tion-al) to ease phonological decoding.
  • Word-Box Isolation: Isolates the active hovered word in a prominent contrast card.
Figure 2: Active Sage Green calming tint with anchored OpenDyslexic letterforms and accommodation status toasts.
Figure 3: Active Reading Ruler isolating the reading line while dimming peripheral text to prevent visual drift.
Dyslexia Assistant • Writing & Learning Writer & Flashcards

4. Distraction-Free Writer & Readability Analyzer

Writing presents immense friction for individuals with dyslexia. Dyslexia Assistant's Writer provides a therapeutic writing space with assistive technology built directly into the editor.

Key Writer Features:

  • Speech-to-Text Dictation: Allows students to articulate their thoughts freely without being hindered by spelling struggles.
  • Auditory Proofreading ("Read Back"): High-fidelity local speech synthesis reads back drafted text so students can hear mistakes.
  • Real-time Readability Scoring: Live metrics compute Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and reading duration.

Export & Interoperability:

  • Clean PDF Export: Exports essays and homework to pristine print-ready PDFs stripping out all UI chrome.
  • Markdown Export: Exports structured text for documentation and school submissions.
  • Local Document Management: Autosaves drafts securely in browser storage.
Figure 4: The Writer workspace showing word counts, grade level metrics, speech dictation, and export actions.

Dyslexia Assistant • Educator Integration Sharing & Gamification

6. Teacher & Student One-Click Lesson Sharing

Special education teachers and parents can create customized reading passages and instantly share them with students without requiring accounts or logins.

Zero-Setup Lesson Distribution

  • Accommodation Presets Encoded in URL: The share engine embeds font size, tint, and typography directly into the URL query.
  • 1-Click Instant Actions: Teachers can send links directly to parents or classroom groups via WhatsApp, Email, or LMS.
  • Frictionless Student Access: When the student clicks the link, the passage opens in Reader mode with the exact specified visual accommodations already configured.
FERPA & COPPA Aligned: Because the URL itself holds the encoded passage, no student identification or lesson data is logged or retained on any third-party server.
Figure 6: One-click teacher lesson sharing modal with URL generation and instant messaging distribution.

7. Gamified Progress & Streak Tracking

Positive reinforcement is vital for dyslexic learners who frequently experience academic frustration. The progress engine turns daily reading into a rewarding journey.

Empowering Superpower Badges:

  • First Step: Unlocked upon completing the first reading session.
  • Page Turner: Reached after reading 500 cumulative words.
  • Focus Flame: Maintained through daily consecutive study streaks.
  • Super Scholar: Earned upon completing 2,000 words.
  • Deep Listener: Unlocked by completing 5 speech-assisted sessions.
Figure 7: Daily streak dashboard displaying words read, focus timer, and earned dyslexia superpower badges.
Dyslexia Assistant • Accessibility & Compliance Standards & Guide

8. Lexi the Wise Owl: Voice-Guided Onboarding

Complex assistive toolbars can overwhelm neurodivergent users. Lexi, our interactive owl mascot, provides an empathetic, 6-step spoken guided tour through the application.

Inclusive Onboarding Design:

  • Auditory + Visual Synchrony: Lexi speaks aloud using speech synthesis while simultaneously highlighting relevant buttons.
  • Gentle Pacing: Students can progress through the 6 tour cards at their own speed or skip at any point.
  • Non-Intrusive Testing Guards: The tour automatically respects automated screen reader contexts and testing environments.
Figure 8: Lexi the Wise Owl guiding a new learner through tint selection and focus tools.
